name: Spacemud
english_description: A space-themed fork of the LIMA Mudlib (the same FluffOS reference framework already onboarded standalone as libs/lima) that keeps Lima's engine -- natural-language command parsing ('take the red potion from the box'), capability-based security, Unix-like wizard shell -- but swaps its fantasy wizard's-guildhall demo world for a decaying, nine-floor space station called Omega. A fresh character wakes up there and can wander its maintenance corridors, waiting rooms, and a domed Stargate Terminal (a pulsating circular teleport platform under a star-filled skylight) run by chief landing controller Aria Voss and a small cast of named station staff (Doc Green, Doc Williams, Rigel Fluxx, Zara Nebulon, Max Nova); the Yakitori delivery guild runs its own chef/cashier counter selling skewer snacks, tech gremlins and space roaches skitter the lower decks, and a lunar lurker mob and salvageable hyperspace hoodie armour round out Omega's authored content. Underneath the station sits a from-scratch procedural-universe layer (space_d/ship_d/spacestation_d/proc_gen_d) that generates star systems and planets at first boot -- Greek-alphabet naming conventions, gravity/mass/radius stats -- meant to support the game's real ambition per its own README: fly a purchased spacecraft, haul and sell goods, dock at stations, and eventually manage planet-side corporations, layered on top of a genuine crafting/salvage system (break weapons and armour into scrap metal, cloth, and plastics at any workbench). The parallel domains/pinto directory is not spacemud's own content -- it's LimaLib's official docs.limalib.dev tutorial reference code (a single swamp room and a swan NPC), bundled for readers following the upstream learning path rather than a second game area. Onboarding fixed two severe, previously-uncatalogued engine bugs that had silently broken this content mudlib-wide since first boot -- a check_privilege()-gated call fired straight from create() (impossible to pass with no connected player yet), which killed every complex-exit 'go' method (all elevators/doors) and blocked the procedural universe from ever generating; and a mapping-identity-vs-value equality bug in the crafting daemon that made every single salvage attempt fail with 'Invalid salvage type' -- plus several smaller content/compat fixes (an account-menu crash for non-xterm256 clients, a stale content path, two US/UK spelling typos, a missing header blocking two Omega terminal items). Full registration-to-gameplay playthrough verified live, including the station wakeup room, the elevator/door fix, and a real armour-salvage round-trip. First character auto-granted wizard/admin per Lima's own documented AUTO_WIZ convention. See libs/spacemud/NOTES.md and AGENTS.md #7.166/#7.167 for the full technical writeup.
